Make APM deviation window alignment errors actionable

**Not merge-ready: eval gate remains open.** The [completed re-QA on `c080d386`](https://github.com/last9/last9-mcp-server/pull/507#issuecomment-6637378025) is **FAIL** and supersedes the earlier PASS that waived evals. OpenAI evals did run with `EVAL_OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini`: `slad-003` was confirmed as a regression (PR 1/10 vs main 3/10); `lpa-001` was classified as noise (PR 5/10 vs main 2/10). The reviewer reports that qamcp resume-safety left the old PASS in place because no same-head override exists; that stale verdict must not authorize merging. Current head `29de1e8f` has no fresh live eval verdict.

Explicit current and baseline window alignment errors now report the query step and nearest aligned start/end arguments, so callers can correct their timestamps and retry. Invalid explicit windows remain rejected. The changelog records this behavior.

`TestResolveDeviationWindowsUnalignedErrorNamesStepAndNearestAlignedWindow` reproduced the generic error before the fix and passes afterward. Its six cases cover both windows, rounding down/up, an unaligned end, sub-step windows, and a 300-second step.

Following the [eval comparison](https://github.com/last9/last9-mcp-server/pull/507#issuecomment-6637254398), commit `29de1e8f` restores the APM description byte-for-byte to baseline `31a1829`. This removes the PR's only tool-description delta while retaining the runtime diagnostic fix. The existing description remains accurate. No new unit test was added for this markdown-only restoration: a before/after comparison of `dump-tools --toolsets=investigate` failed before it (only the APM description differed) and passed afterward. All 42 tools and initialize instructions now match the eval baseline byte-for-byte; both dumps have SHA-256 `824c6053d76539d83e1d002f2b610d39491a41a9ec400f7fc35970034aa8d54d`.

Local validation: `go build .`, `go test ./internal/apm ./internal/prompts -count=1`, focused root dump/metadata/routing tests, `make lint-test`, `go vet ./internal/apm ./internal/prompts`, formatting and diff checks passed. The focused package tests also passed independently at the new commit. Full suite, race, integration and live evals remain with CI/the orchestrator; supplied CI state is skipped.

[Live QA on c080d38](https://github.com/last9/last9-mcp-server/pull/507#issuecomment-6632135932) passed alignment diagnostics, snap-and-retry, aligned controls, lookback alignment, negative inputs, toolset routing, A/A and dimension-isolation checks. That evidence predates the description restoration. The live query step is 60 seconds; 300 seconds is unit-tested only. Backend string lookup was waived because the QA backend checkout was unavailable. QA also recorded pre-existing aggregate-versus-range oracle discrepancies and fleet/multi-environment responses above 32 KB; no writes or leftovers were reported.

The subsequently completed eval comparison supersedes the earlier missing-model blocker: at ten runs, `lpa-001` was classified as noise (candidate 5/10 vs baseline 2/10), while `slad-003` was reported as a regression (1/10 vs 3/10). Metadata equality is not a live eval pass. QA/orchestrator must rerun the same OpenAI backend with `EVAL_OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini`, investigate toolset, suites and ten-run confirmation on `29de1e8f` versus `31a1829`, recording pass rates and tool-call counts and publishing a current-head verdict before clearing that gate.

The npm-wrapper preparation failed because its staging directory lacked `bin/download-binary.js`; Go build and validation were unaffected.

This review follow-up changes PR metadata only; no runtime behavior changed and no new regression test applies. Rechecked locally: `go test ./internal/apm -run TestResolveDeviationWindows -count=1`, `go build .`, and `make lint-test` passed; `git diff --exit-code 31a1829a HEAD -- internal/prompts` confirmed baseline prompt equality. Live evals remain with QA/orchestrator: this environment has no eval checkout, OpenAI/Last9 credentials, or local dotenv.

Fixes #506

Bound get_logs adaptive chunk plans before dispatch

`get_logs` now rejects adaptive raw-search plans above 24 chunks before allocating chunks or sending log queries. The error reports the planned count and tells callers to narrow lookback_minutes to 1440 or the absolute window to 24 hours, without retrying unchanged. The logjson reference documents the budget.

Previously, bounded concurrency still allowed a seven-day raw query to issue 168 requests. This cap bounds total request amplification while preserving single-request aggregate and server-side search paths and existing fail-closed chunk handling. Admitted queries can still time out.

Validation: `TestGetLogsChunkBudget` was observed failing with 25, 48 and 168 upstream requests, and `TestGetLogsChunkBudgetReturnsRewriteToolError` with successful empty data. Both pass with the fix. Coverage includes 23/24/25 chunks, a one-millisecond boundary overrun, single-request exemptions, zero requests on refusal, and caller-fixable MCP error guidance.

After reconciling both main-merge histories at `a8111403`, passed locally:
- `go test ./internal/telemetry/logs ./internal/prompts -count=1`
- Focused root tests for chunk-budget refusal, stalled-query deadline, tool metadata, reference resources, server instructions, dump-tools, comment lint and goroutine lint.
- `go build .`, `go vet . ./internal/telemetry/logs ./internal/prompts`, gofmt and `git diff --check`.
- Focused per-commit checks on both unpushed merge commits, without rebasing.

[Live QA reported PASS on 3caf17e](https://github.com/last9/last9-mcp-server/pull/510#issuecomment-6638689904), with the induced mid-window fault check waived on that host. Full-suite, race and integration validation of the merged head remain for CI. No new test was needed for the history-only reconciliation. The harness npm preparation failed because its environment directory lacked `bin/download-binary.js`; Go checks were unaffected.

Fixes #509

Measure that an HCL document claims no node it does not name

G119 of stokaro/ptah#4204, the plugin half. The host half, stokaro/ptah#5329, is merged.

An HCL document is an Atlas file, which names none of the coordination nodes it leaves out. The host's built-in engine reads a document without a `coordination_node` header entry as claiming no node. On the provider path the same document planned to drop every node it did not declare: `schema "<dir>" {}` applied with `--schemas <dir>` over a directory holding node `plain` planned `<dir>.plain: Drops the node and its runtime coordination state (destructive)`.

The plan was for the provider to claim the nodes only from a `coordination_node` limit. The SDK does not allow it: `validateSourceCoverage` requires every model of a document without header limits to be COMPLETE, and both the provider's runtime and the host's client check the reply. The provider already narrows its claim from limits where a document has them (`limitedClaim`). So the rule sits in the host (stokaro/ptah#5329): the host asks the provider about an HCL document only when the header holds one of the engine's header kinds, and an HCL export writes the captured `ptah:feature-coverage` header so the export keeps its claim. This pull request changes no provider behavior. It adds the live tests, states the rule in the README, and notes it at `limitedClaim`.

## Tests

`integration/host_hcl_claim_test.go`:

- `TestHostKeepsTheNodesAnHCLDocumentDoesNotName`: over a directory holding `plain`, `schema "<dir>" {}` plans nothing; a document that declares `other` plans only its creation; a document whose header names another node (`// ptah:not-described coordination_node "<dir>/unmanaged"`) claims the rest and plans the drop of `plain`.
- `TestHostTakesAnHCLExportsClaimFromItsHeader`: an export without its header and without the node's block plans nothing; with the header and without the block it drops the node.

Both skip on a host whose HCL export of a directory holding a node writes the node and no `ptah:feature-coverage` header. That is the exact output of the release host (v0.21.0), and of host master before stokaro/ptah#5329; any other answer fails the test. `TestHostAppliesAnHCLExportOfADirectoryAsComplete` is unchanged and holds on both kinds of host: through the provider's complete reply on the old one, through the header on the new one.

## Measured on local-ydb 26.2.1.14

- Host branch of stokaro/ptah#5329: both new tests pass, and so do the existing HCL and export tests (`TestHostAppliesAnHCLExportOfADirectoryAsComplete`, the Go export tests, `TestHostExportsAGoSourceAsHCLSubprocess`, `TestHostReplansAnExportedReadSubprocess`, `TestHostExportRefusesANullableKeyColumnSubprocess`, the HCL rebuild tests).
- v0.21.0 and host master: `TestHostTakesAnHCLExportsClaimFromItsHeader` skips with the probe's message. In those local runs the other test stopped earlier, at a cold provider start; the release and master legs here are its evidence.

## Verify

```sh
PTAH_YDB_TEST_URL=... PTAH_HOST_TEST_BIN=<ptah built from stokaro/ptah#5329> \
  GOWORK=off go test -tags integration ./integration -count=1 -v \
  -run 'TestHostKeepsTheNodesAnHCLDocumentDoesNotName|TestHostTakesAnHCLExportsClaimFromItsHeader'
```

## CI

With `.github/host-ref` naming the host branch, every blocking leg passed: release and host branch, on 25.1.4.7 and 26.2.1.14. Both new tests passed on the host-branch legs and skipped on the release legs. The file is removed now that the host change is merged. The master leg fails on post-flip host failures that this change does not touch, and both new tests skipped there before the merge.

Ablation, on vcluster at 26.2.1.14: the host branch built without its header check fails both new tests on the planned drop (`coordination-node-operation <dir>.plain`, `<dir>.local`). The probe does not skip there, because that host still writes the header.

diff --git a/integration/host_hcl_claim_test.go b/integration/host_hcl_claim_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..941707e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/integration/host_hcl_claim_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+//go:build integration
+
+package integration_test
+
+import (
+	"path"
+	"regexp"
+	"testing"
+
+	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
+	"github.com/stokaro/ptah-ydb-plugin/internal/testcheck"
+)
+
+// The tests here plan HCL documents through the host with this provider
+// selected. An HCL document is an Atlas file, which names none of the
+// coordination nodes it leaves out, so it claims the nodes only through its
+// header, as the host's embedded YDB engine reads it: a coordination_node
+// entry, or the captured ptah:feature-coverage header an export writes. A
+// document with neither drops no node.
+
+// coverageHeaderLine matches the captured feature coverage header line of an
+// HCL document.
+var coverageHeaderLine = regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^// ptah:feature-coverage \{.*\}\n`)
+
+// hclExportWithClaim exports the directory as HCL through the host and
+// returns the document, which declares node. The test is skipped on a host
+// that writes the export without a captured feature coverage header: such a
+// host takes an HCL document's claim of the nodes from the provider's reply,
+// which the SDK makes complete for a document without header limits, so a
+// plan from any HCL document drops the nodes it does not declare. Any other
+// answer fails the test.
+func hclExportWithClaim(c *qt.C, directory, node string) string {
+	c.Helper()
+	document, _ := hostExport(c, "schema", "inspect", "--schemas", directory, "--format", "hcl")
+	c.Assert(document, qt.Matches, `(?s).*coordination_node "`+regexp.QuoteMeta(node)+`" \{.*`, qt.Commentf("%s", document))
+	if !coverageHeaderLine.MatchString(document) {
+		c.Skip("the selected host writes this provider's HCL export without a ptah:feature-coverage header, " +
+			"and takes an HCL document's claim of the nodes from the provider's complete reply")
+	}
+	return document
+}
+
+// An HCL document that declares the directory and no node plans nothing over
+// a directory that holds one, and one that declares another node only creates
+// it: neither claims the nodes it does not name. With a coordination_node
+// header entry that names another node, the document claims the rest, and the
+// plan drops the node it leaves out.
+func TestHostKeepsTheNodesAnHCLDocumentDoesNotName(t *testing.T) {
+	c := testcheck.New(t)
+	opened, directory, database := lockFixture(c)
+	createNode(c, opened, path.Join(database, directory, "plain"))
+	hclExportWithClaim(c, directory, "plain")
+	empty := `schema "` + directory + `" {}` + "\n"
+	another := empty + `coordination_node "` + directory + `" "other" {}` + "\n"
+	claimed := `// ptah:not-described coordination_node "` + directory + `/unmanaged"` + "\n" + empty
+
+	c.Assert(hostPlanned(c, directory, "hcl", empty), qt.HasLen, 0)
+	c.Assert(hostPlanned(c, directory, "hcl", another), qt.DeepEquals, []string{"coordination-node-operation " + directory + ".other"})
+	c.Assert(hostPlanned(c, directory, "hcl", claimed), qt.DeepEquals, []string{"coordination-node-operation " + directory + ".plain"})
+}
+
+// An HCL export of a directory claims its nodes through its captured header:
+// without the header and a node's block it plans nothing, and with the header
+// and without the block it drops the node.
+func TestHostTakesAnHCLExportsClaimFromItsHeader(t *testing.T) {
+	c := testcheck.New(t)
+	opened, directory, database := lockFixture(c)
+	createNode(c, opened, path.Join(database, directory, "local"))
+	document := hclExportWithClaim(c, directory, "local")
+	block := regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)coordination_node "local" \{.*?\n\}\n`)
+	withoutBlock := block.ReplaceAllString(document, "")
+	withoutEither := coverageHeaderLine.ReplaceAllString(withoutBlock, "")
+
+	c.Assert(withoutBlock, qt.Not(qt.Equals), document)
+	c.Assert(withoutEither, qt.Not(qt.Equals), withoutBlock)
+	c.Assert(hostPlanned(c, directory, "hcl", withoutEither), qt.HasLen, 0, qt.Commentf("%s", withoutEither))
+	c.Assert(hostPlanned(c, directory, "hcl", withoutBlock), qt.DeepEquals, []string{"coordination-node-operation " + directory + ".local"},
+		qt.Commentf("%s", withoutBlock))
+}
